heard: Standing on the tallest mountain, you wouldn't know you were on one. In 1971, the Mariner 9 spacecraft arrived in orbit and confirmed Nix-Olympica as a massive volcano. Olympus Mons stands approximately 21 to 25 kilometers high on the Martian surface. That is roughly three times the height of Mount Everest, spreading as wide as the state of Arizona. Yet its shield volcano profile has an average slope of just five percent. Because of this gentle grade, the ground appears as a plane stretching to a horizon a mere three kilometers away. The summit calderas remain completely out of view, hiding the scale of the largest volcano in the solar system. That is why standing on the tallest mountain, you wouldn't know you were on one.
